rationale: Both use the same correct brute-force loop over a <= b and track min and max as they go. B marks whether min and max have been set with explicit minSet/maxSet flags. A infers that from len(Factorizations) == 0, which works but is more implicit. B's reset-then-append pattern also avoids repeating the factor-pair literal in two branches. B's isPalindrome reverses the number arithmetically and documents that negatives are rejected, so it needs no string allocation. A's string-based check is equally clear. B has a minor inconsistency: it uses fmt.Errorf with no formatting in one place and errors.New in another. Both shadow the min/max builtins. On balance B's state handling is slightly clearer and more robust.
